items.title: Should You Buy Medtronic Stock as Its Hugo Surgical Robot Gains Ground?
items.summary: The company is in the process of expanding the uses for its Hugo Surgical System and expanding its revenue base.

items.title: Is ISRG Stock Really As Expensive As It Looks?
items.summary: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), maker of the da Vinci surgical robots, trades at about $382, some 36% below its 52-week high. Even so, you pay about 35.9 times trailing adjusted earnings. That is normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back, a basis meant to sit closer to the one analysts forecast on, though the two are not defined identically. Analysts' forecasts run to 2027, the year Intuitive plans to start lowering what customers pay per use on some instruments.

items.title: Why BSX Stock Lost More Than Half Its Value While Sales Kept Rising
items.summary: Boston Scientific (BSX) has fallen about 54% since late December 2025, and it now sits at $43.91, just above a 52-week low of $42.63. Device peers were mixed over the same nine months: Abbott lost about 17%, Medtronic barely moved, and Johnson & Johnson rose about 32%. The market repriced Boston Scientific's growth rate after management concentrated its guidance cut in two core product lines.

items.title: Medtronic (MDT) Raises its Outlook Again as Heart Device Demand Keeps Climbing

items.title: BSX vs. MDT: Which Electrophysiology Stock Is the Better Bet Now?
items.summary: Boston Scientific faces near-term pressure in electrophysiology, while Medtronic gains share and sees stronger momentum across key franchises.

items.title: FDA clears vessel-sealing device for Medtronic’s Hugo robot
items.summary: Widely adopted in open and laparoscopic surgeries, the LigaSure instrument is now available for use with the Hugo robotic system.

items.title: Should You Judge JNJ Stock Without STELARA?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) has been a rewarding stock to hold, up about 53% over the past year against about 17% for the S&P 500. The change worth noticing over that stretch is quieter than the price. Management said sales still rose 5.6% despite a STELARA drag of about 460 basis points. Management is encouraging investors to evaluate the company's underlying momentum by presenting growth rates that exclude STELARA alongside its reported figures.

items.title: Recor Medical ex-CEO Lara Barghout joins Medtronic
items.summary: Barghout, who led Recor when it won FDA approval of the first renal denervation treatment for hypertension, is the new president of Medtronic’s Interventional Cardiology Therapies business.
